title: Personal Showreel
concept:
A curated selection of my work in video editing and motion design, exploring different visual styles, creative approaches, and storytelling techniques.

Let's create something great together.

title: AI Century – Commercial Reel
concept:
An end-to-end commercial project for AI Century, built around a clean, Apple-inspired SaaS visual aesthetic.

Starting from the initial concept and creative direction through to final production, the video breaks down the platform's features into clear, visually engaging segments, demonstrating what the product can do and how it delivers value.

title: The Life & Career of Macaulay Culkin (Test Project)
concept:
A documentary-style motion design project exploring the life and career of Macaulay Culkin, created as a trial project for Ming.

Following the provided script, I developed a series of detailed animations and visual sequences inspired by Vox-style editorial storytelling. The visual direction combines expressive typography, layered paper textures, VHS aesthetics, and vintage-inspired elements to create a nostalgic, archival feel while keeping the narrative engaging and visually cohesive.

title: Trip.com – Brand Concept & Commercial
concept:
An independent concept project exploring a fresh visual direction for Trip.com and its digital travel platform.

Developed entirely from concept to final production, the project reimagines the brand through an Apple-inspired design approach, combining clean layouts, refined typography, and modern SaaS aesthetics with alternative visual styles to explore new possibilities for the brand's identity and communication.

title: Language Learning – Social Media Ads
concept:
A series of short-form video ads created for Migaku, promoting its language learning platform across Meta advertising channels.

Focused on performance-driven editing, the videos combine engaging hooks, dynamic pacing, and clear product demonstrations to communicate the platform's features and value, turning language learning experiences into compelling advertising content.

title: AI Tutorial – End-to-End Production
role: Content Strategy, AI Workflow Development & Video Production
tools: Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, Claude, OpenArt
concept:
An end-to-end educational content project for AI Century, covering the entire production process from niche research and content ideation to AI workflow development and final video production.

I developed the tutorial concepts, created custom AI workflows and skills, explored AI-powered tools to generate visual assets, and structured the scripts and step-by-step instructions to make complex workflows accessible and engaging.

The final videos combine practical demonstrations, visual storytelling, and carefully paced editing to turn creative AI processes into easy-to-follow educational content.

title: Street Portraits – Short-Form Content
concept:
A short-form video editing project for artist and content creator Whit, featuring spontaneous portrait-drawing interactions with strangers in shopping malls.

Working with provided footage, I crafted engaging narratives through strong opening hooks, clear storytelling, and carefully structured pacing. The editing highlights genuine human interactions and emotional moments while maintaining a consistent, repeatable content format designed for short-form platforms.

The goal was to transform raw footage into accessible, engaging stories that capture attention and keep viewers watching.

title: Viral Video Recreation – Short-Form
concept:
A short-form educational video demonstrating how viral video clips can be recreated using AI-powered tools and creative techniques.

Focused on clear, engaging editing, the video breaks down the recreation process into easy-to-follow steps, helping viewers understand how to replicate popular visual trends and recreate viral content themselves.

title: Human Stories – Interview Feature
concept:
An interview-based video project featuring a chef, exploring the personal stories and experiences behind an ordinary individual's life.

Combining filming and editing, I selected compelling questions and meaningful moments from the original interview to create a curated video feature. Through thoughtful pacing, music, and visual storytelling, the project aims to spark curiosity, reveal the human stories behind everyday people, and make their experiences engaging and relatable to audiences.

title: Viral Video Recreation – YouTube Tutorial
concept:
A long-form YouTube tutorial demonstrating how to recreate viral video content using AI-powered tools and creative workflows.

Focused on educational storytelling and structured editing, the video guides viewers through the recreation process step by step, combining practical demonstrations, visual explanations, and clear pacing to make complex techniques accessible and easy to follow.

The goal is to help viewers understand not just how viral content is made, but how they can recreate it themselves.

title: Food Safety – Documentary Feature (Test Project)
concept:
A documentary-style video project exploring food safety issues, developed as a trial project for SteveGagz.

Inspired by Vox-style editorial storytelling, the video combines carefully selected B-roll footage, archival imagery, and custom motion graphics to illustrate key points and make complex information easier to understand.

Through purposeful visual storytelling, typography, and well-paced editing, the goal is to transform information-heavy topics into engaging and accessible documentary content.

title: Lifestyle Vlog – Short-form Storytelling
concept:
A lifestyle vlog editing project focused on transforming everyday moments and scattered footage into engaging, entertaining visual stories.

Through thoughtful storytelling, expressive typography, music, B-roll, and motion graphics, I bring structure and personality to ordinary daily experiences.

With a strong focus on comedic timing, pacing, and emotional rhythm, the editing creates a lighthearted and entertaining viewing experience that keeps audiences engaged and wanting to watch more.
